observations: Photo 0 shows a pair of automotive headlights with integrated indicators.
Photo 1 shows a vehicle front grill with vertical slats and a central Toyota emblem.
The headlight lenses in photo 0 appear cloudy or yellowed, suggesting oxidation.
The floor tiles are consistent across both photos, suggesting they were taken in the same location.
The seller's text identifies the items as 'tailight' but photo 0 clearly shows headlights.

claims.evidence: The grill and headlight design are a visual match for the Toyota Land Cruiser Prado 120 series.
Electrical components and bulb integrity cannot be tested through photos.

risks.risk: Internal electrical failure or missing bulbs
risks.proof: A video showing both headlights connected to a power source and fully illuminated (high/low beam and indicators).
Clear photos of the rear and sides of the grill and both headlights showing all plastic mounting points.
risks.if_unproven: as having broken tabs requiring adhesive or modification to install

risks.risk: Permanent lens damage or deep scratches
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the headlight lenses after being wiped with a damp cloth.

proof_requests: Video of the headlights powered on to confirm bulbs and internal wiring work.
Photos of the back of the grill and headlights to check for broken mounting clips.
Confirmation if the seller actually has taillights, as the photo shows headlights.
response.reason: The items are clearly identifiable as Toyota Prado J120 parts. Despite the seller mislabeling the headlights as taillights, the physical goods are visible and can be priced at their worst-case used condition.
